data.hypothesis: A 16-byte SSE2 mask validator may reduce scalar control flow on the official mixed-width n=65536 input by classifying every byte lane, comparing continuation masks against shifted starter requirements with carry across blocks, and checking restricted second-byte ranges. A bounded scalar fallback from the last known code-point boundary handles the tail and any unfinished sequence. The SSE2 path is enabled only when the compiler target defines __SSE2__; otherwise the supplied scalar validator remains the control. This is a performance hypothesis, not a claimed speedup.
data.notes: The baseline measured 49.62 µs; the prior 64-bit ASCII-block/scalar hybrid measured 57.50 µs, and prior SWAR mask variants failed correctness checks. This candidate is distinct and unmeasured; the controller must evaluate correctness and speed, including vector boundaries and truncations.
transformations: Retained the supplied scalar validator as a control and fallback.
Added compile-time guarded 16-byte SSE2 lane classification for ASCII, continuation bytes, and legal two-, three-, and four-byte starters.
Compared shifted starter requirements with continuation masks while carrying cross-block continuation state.
Checked E0, ED, F0, and F4 second-byte bounds, including a pending bound at vector boundaries.
Used scalar validation from the last known code-point boundary for an incomplete vector tail; preserved the run ABI, output, and thread budget.
